subject.title: feat: add readiness conditions and providers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `gateway.readiness`, `registerReadinessCriterion`, and the `ready` RPC/CLI as permanent core and public Plugin SDK contracts with opt-in fail-closed criteria?
rationale: Tests and runtime proof can establish implementation behavior, but they cannot decide whether these configuration identities, plugin callbacks, condition vocabulary, and availability semantics should become long-lived public product contracts.

options.title: Approve the bounded readiness slice
options.body: Accept the proposed opt-in contracts, then require a current-main rebase and refreshed exact-head runtime and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Land canonical core conditions and the CLI projection first while deferring plugin registration and operator-selected criteria until their API design is separately approved.

options.title: Wait for RFC acceptance
options.body: Pause this PR until the linked RFC settles condition identities, plugin ownership, and fail-closed semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded readiness slice
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed opt-in contracts, then require a current-main rebase and refreshed exact-head runtime and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the existing channel-backed readiness implementation and adjacent Gateway readiness ownership.
